findings.layer: R127 restricted token vs Electron 43 node bootstrap
findings.summary: Electron aborts startup because platform_util::IsNulDeviceEnabled performs _open("nul", _O_RDWR) and WRITE_RESTRICTED denies every write open of the nul device.
findings.child_stderr: [FATAL:electron\shell\common\node_bindings.cc:735] Unable to open nul device needed for initialization,aborting startup. As a workaround, try starting with --no-stdio-init
findings.mechanism: Measured with isolated probe children on the production spawn path: read open succeeds, write and read+write opens return ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (5) under the restricted token and all three succeed under the normal token.
findings.fix: Windows-only --no-stdio-init appended after the shared engine argument set.
findings.fix_justification: Pinned sources: electron v43.3.0 node_bindings.cc gates only the fail-fast probe on the switch; node v24.18.1 src/node.cc shows kNoStdioInitialization on Windows disables only (1) that probe, (2) the fd 0-2 repair loop that opens nul when a handle is missing or FILE_TYPE_UNKNOWN, and (3) atexit(ResetStdio) whose Windows body is uv_tty_reset_mode(). spawn_restricted always supplies three valid handles through STARTF_USESTDHANDLES and never attaches a console, and Electron copies the switch to renderer and utility children via kCommonSwitchNames.
findings.verified: child stderr FATAL disappears and startup proceeds to the next stage

findings.layer: Electron 43 on Windows vs the shim stdin boot capability
findings.summary: Electron replaces process.stdin on Windows with an already-ended, non-configurable Readable, so readBootCapability() observes zero bytes and bootstrap fails before either pipe is connected.

findings.why_not_committed: the task explicitly excludes shim changes, and the change alters app.asar bytes and asar_header_sha256 on every platform, which would invalidate the pinned macOS artifact evidence; blocker E2-3 keeps Windows failing regardless

findings.layer: Chromium Mojo IPC vs R127 WRITE_RESTRICTED primary token
findings.summary: mojo::PlatformChannel::CreateChannel creates a named pipe with the default security descriptor and immediately reopens it with GENERIC_READ | GENERIC_WRITE; NPFS does not copy the token default DACL, so the object never names the Restricted Code SID and the write open is refused.
findings.surfaced_after: E2-1 fix plus the E2-2 candidate fix; the engine then reaches start and reports load_timeout
findings.mechanism: Same restricting-SID asymmetry as E2-1 but inside Chromium's own IPC backbone; the project cannot change the Chromium call, and removing the token/Job/ACL, enabling breakaway, editing host device or NPFS ACLs, adding a broad restricting SID, or downgrading the limit to a warning are all forbidden by the task.
